learning_outcomes.text: Knows the principles, methods, and stages of the computer-aided design process used in mechanical engineering.
Explains the principles of 2D and 3D modeling, generation of part assemblies in professional CAD environments (CATIA, SolidWorks, Autodesk Inventor etc.).
Identifies and applies national and international standards (ISO, EN) regarding technical drawings, tolerances, fits, and surface roughness.
Knows methods for geometric and functional analysis of mechanical components for optimizing construction and manufacturing processes.
Develops 3D models of complex mechanical parts and assemblies using computer-aided design tools.
Applies procedures for assembly, dimensioning, and automatic generation of technical documentation (production and assembly drawings).
Uses simulation, analysis, and verification functions in a CAD environment to evaluate the structural behavior of components.
Selects and applies appropriate methods for representing and dimensioning machine elements in technical production drawings.
Plans and individually manages the design, modeling, and technical documentation stages of a mechanical product.
Demonstrates autonomy in carrying out CAD projects, respecting quality, ergonomics, and safety standards.
Demonstrates professional responsibility in using design software, respecting professional ethics and intellectual property legislation.
Critically evaluates own models and technical documentation, identifying errors and proposing optimization solutions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: General criteria and design environments. Planar sketches. Construction and editing.
3D modeling of parts with dimensionally homogeneous geometry - Planar sketching elements. Differences from AutoCAD; Graphic and geometric transformations in plane.
Primary editing of 3D parts - Direct generation procedures; Indirect generation procedures.
Secondary editing of 3D parts - Implicit editing: Edge Fillet, Chamfer, Mirror, Scale etc.; Explicit editing: Groove, Pocket etc.
Drawing-type documents, for parts and assemblies - Traced production drawings; Computer-created production drawings, based on the model; Elements of dimensional precision and surface quality.
Draft procedures: Production drawings (representation, sections, details, supplementary views)
Draft procedures: Production drawings (deviations, fits, tolerances, roughness etc.)
Draft procedures: Production drawings (dimensioning of machine elements)
teaching_methods: Free exposition supported by computer and video projector (lectures and labs)
Individual problem-solving on computer using CATIA V5 software during laboratory sessions

assessment_methods.method: Formative assessment test (checks during the semester)
Laboratory activity (completion of all laboratory works)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades will be awarded as integers from 1 to 10. A grade of 5 certifies the achievement of minimal learning outcomes and the award of corresponding study credits. A minimum score of 5 is required for each assessment component.
